oneLiner: The broadest semiconductor equipment franchise just printed a record quarter and guided Q4 revenue up 51% - and the stock fell 5%, because a 50x trailing multiple had already priced the beat.
thesis: AI capex is inflecting AMAT's growth. Q3 FY26 revenue hit a record $9.115B (+25% YoY, +15% QoQ) and management guided Q4 to $10.25B (+51% YoY) with EPS +85% - a step-change acceleration, not a cyclical wiggle.
The CY26 outlook keeps rising. Management raised its calendar-2026 semiconductor equipment growth outlook to 30%+ (from 20%+ in February), with advanced packaging revenue guided to grow 50%+.

Leverage to GAA and HBM. Materials-engineering intensity rises with gate-all-around transistors, backside power, and HBM stacking; Semiconductor Systems did $7.04B in Q3 FY26 vs $5.56B a year earlier, and EPIC partnerships span TSMC, Samsung, SK hynix, and Micron.
Services compound quietly. AGS hit a record $1.8B in Q3 FY26, +22% YoY - a recurring-revenue ballast on a massive installed base.
Cash conversion snapped back. After Q2's deliberate inventory build crushed FCF to $210M, Q3 delivered record operating cash flow above $3B and FCF of $2.3B.

latestProse: Q3 FY26 (reported Aug 13, 2026) was a record: revenue of $9.115B rose 25% YoY and 15% sequentially, non-GAAP gross margin ticked up to 50.4%, and non-GAAP EPS of $3.50 beat both the $3.36 guide and consensus. Semiconductor Systems did $7.04B versus $5.56B a year earlier, AGS hit a record $1.8B (+22%), and cash conversion snapped back hard - record operating cash flow above $3B with $2.3B of free cash flow after Q2's inventory-build trough. Yet the stock fell roughly 5% on Aug 14: analysts flagged near-term gross-margin headwinds from accelerating capex and headcount expansion, and a China mix that contracted to about 28% of sales under export controls. The disclosure that matters most: the Q4 guide of $10.25B and $4.02 EPS implies 51% revenue and 85% EPS growth - an acceleration so steep the market's first question was how long it can possibly be sustained.
guidanceProse: Q4 FY26 guidance: revenue $10.25B plus or minus $500M (+51% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS $4.02 plus or minus $0.20 (+85% YoY) - far above the pre-print trajectory and confirming the CY26 equipment growth outlook of 30%+ with packaging growing 50%+. Management pointed to continued demand across DRAM, leading-edge foundry-logic, and advanced packaging. The post-print debate shifted from whether the acceleration is real to whether margins hold: guidance embeds heavier spending (capex, headcount) into the ramp, and the November print brings the first formal CY2027 commentary against SEMI's +~22% 2027 WFE forecast, with China (~28% of sales) still exposed to the suspended BIS affiliates rule and the pending MATCH Act.

guide.label: Q4 FY26 revenue guide
guide.sub: EPS $4.02 +/-$0.20; +51% revenue and +85% EPS YoY; results Nov 2026

segments: Semiconductor Systems: $7.04B, ~77% of Q3 FY26 revenue (vs $5.56B a year earlier)
Applied Global Services: record $1.8B, ~20% of revenue, +22% YoY
Display/Other: implied ~$275M residual, ~3%; China cited near 28% of sales (unverified split)
competitive: Lam Research: closest rival in deposition/etch, heavier memory/NAND mix
ASML: litho monopoly captures a growing WFE share; complementary rather than head-on
KLA: process-control leader; Tokyo Electron competes across deposition/etch/clean
AMAT is the largest process-equipment maker by revenue with the broadest portfolio
In advanced packaging, Besi/ASMPT compete in bonding; AMAT is acquiring ASMPT NEXX ($120M, May 2026)
moat: Breadth is the moat: AMAT touches more materials-engineering steps than any rival, and integrated platforms plus co-optimized process flows raise switching costs at GAA/backside-power/HBM inflections. A massive installed base feeds AGS recurring revenue at ~29% operating margins, and the EPIC Center embeds AMAT in customers' next-node R&D.
risks: This is still a cyclical. A Q4 guide of +51% YoY is what cycle peaks look like; SEMI's own 2027-28 deceleration path and any AI capex digestion would compress estimates and the multiple together.
Margin trajectory. The Aug 14 selloff keyed on near-term gross-margin headwinds from accelerating capex and aggressive headcount expansion into the ramp.

China/export-control overhang. China is ~28% of sales and shrinking under controls; the $252.5M BIS penalty is settled, but the suspended affiliates rule could return and the MATCH Act would restrict DUV servicing.
Valuation reset risk. A trailing multiple above 50x into the print left no room for in-line revenue; the stock fell 5% on a record quarter.
Customer concentration. Spending hinges on a handful of buyers (TSMC, Samsung, SK hynix, Micron); a single capex pause is material.
Expectations ratchet. After a ~200% rally into earnings, even $10.25B guided revenue reads as confirmation rather than surprise; the whisper bar now sits above guidance.
catalysts: Nov 2026: Q4 FY26 results and initial CY2027 commentary - the cycle-duration verdict
Fall 2026: hyperscaler 2027 capex guidance as the demand proxy for WFE
H2 2026: MATCH Act progress; any reinstatement of the BIS affiliates rule
Late 2026: SEMI year-end WFE forecast update (2027 currently seen +~22%)
pricedIn: At $507.18 (Aug 14 close, down ~5% post-print from the pre-earnings run; ~$400B market cap), AMAT trades at roughly 30-33x the forward earnings run-rate implied by the Q4 guide (~$16 annualized EPS) - still a re-rated multiple versus the ~20x historical average, but below the 50x+ trailing peak. Consensus target is near $626 (Strong Buy; range roughly $308-900). The market has accepted the AI-secular story; what it has not resolved is whether +51% revenue growth marks mid-cycle or peak, and the 5% post-beat decline says positioning already leans bullish.

scenarios.bear: Q4 margins disappoint on ramp spending, CY27 WFE flattens as AI capex digests, and China restrictions return against a ~28% China mix. EPS estimates stall and the multiple mean-reverts toward mid-20s; stock retraces toward $380-420.
scenarios.base: Q4 lands near the $10.25B guide with EPS ~$4.02, CY26 finishes with equipment growth of 30%+, and November's CY27 commentary pencils in continued growth. The stock recovers toward the ~$626 consensus target.
scenarios.bull: Q4 beats and CY27 WFE guidance confirms SEMI's +22% path (leading-edge logic, HBM/DRAM, packaging +50% compounding); estimates march toward the bullish targets and the stock retests the $700-740 highs.

valPresets.note: Basis is forward earnings: trailing FCF still carries Q2's inventory-build trough (Q3 FCF rebounded to $2.3B), so a trailing FCF-DCF reads more expensive than the business is.
